basis: Total assets as IAS 1 requires the statement of financial position to present it.
caveat: Recognition differs even where the totals are named alike: development costs are capitalised under IAS 38 and generally expensed under ASC 730, and LIFO is permitted under US GAAP and prohibited by IAS 2.

basis: 資産（IFRS）, total assets as a Japanese filer reporting under IFRS presents them.
caveat: A report that prepares consolidated statements states this figure twice, the group's with no dimension on the context and the parent company's own under NonConsolidatedMember, and both are in the table of facts. A query that does not say which it wants gets two sets of accounts at once.

basis: 資産, total assets as the balance sheet of the Ordinance on Financial Statements presents it.
caveat: A report that prepares consolidated statements states this figure twice, the group's with no dimension on the context and the parent company's own under NonConsolidatedMember, and both are in the table of facts. A query that does not say which it wants gets two sets of accounts at once.

basis: Total assets as ASC 210 presents it.
caveat: See the caveat on the IFRS row of this measure.

basis: Cash and cash equivalents as IAS 7 defines them.
caveat: Not directly comparable to the US total: ASU 2016-18 requires restricted cash and restricted cash equivalents in the cash flow statement total, and IAS 7 does not.

basis: 現金及び現金同等物（IFRS）, the balance sheet line.
caveat: A report that prepares consolidated statements states this figure twice, the group's with no dimension on the context and the parent company's own under NonConsolidatedMember, and both are in the table of facts. A query that does not say which it wants gets two sets of accounts at once.

basis: 現金及び現金同等物の残高, the closing balance of the cash flow statement, which is the definition ifrs-full:CashAndCashEquivalents carries.
caveat: A report that prepares consolidated statements states this figure twice, the group's with no dimension on the context and the parent company's own under NonConsolidatedMember, and both are in the table of facts. A query that does not say which it wants gets two sets of accounts at once.

basis: 現金及び預金, the balance sheet line.
caveat: NOT the same figure as the element above it. A Japanese balance sheet presents cash together with deposits, time deposits of more than three months among them, which are not cash equivalents under either framework. It is carried second so that a filer stating no cash flow statement is reached at all, and a figure taken from it should be read as cash and deposits rather than as cash and equivalents. A report that prepares consolidated statements states this figure twice, the group's with no dimension on the context and the parent company's own under NonConsolidatedMember, and both are in the table of facts. A query that does not say which it wants gets two sets of accounts at once.

basis: Cash and cash equivalents excluding restricted amounts; the closer match to IAS 7.
caveat: Excludes restricted cash that the cash flow statement total includes.

basis: The total the cash flow statement reconciles to under ASU 2016-18.
caveat: Includes restricted cash and so overstates the IAS 7 measure.

basis: Total equity including non-controlling interests as IAS 1 presents it.
資本（IFRS）, total equity including the non-controlling interests.
caveat: A report that prepares consolidated statements states this figure twice, the group's with no dimension on the context and the parent company's own under NonConsolidatedMember, and both are in the table of facts. A query that does not say which it wants gets two sets of accounts at once.

basis: 純資産, the net assets, which include the non-controlling interests and the subscription rights to shares; the counterpart of ifrs-full:Equity.
caveat: Japan GAAP has no element for 自己資本, the equity attributable to the parent, which is why no JP-GAAP row defines equity_attributable_to_parent. It is 株主資本 plus 評価・換算差額等 and is a sum rather than a line: taking jppfs_cor:ShareholdersEquity for it is short by the valuation and translation adjustments, which for one report read here is 9,191 million of a correct 63,326 million. A report that prepares consolidated statements states this figure twice, the group's with no dimension on the context and the parent company's own under NonConsolidatedMember, and both are in the table of facts. A query that does not say which it wants gets two sets of accounts at once.

basis: Total equity including non-controlling interests, which is what ifrs-full:Equity means.
Equity attributable to the parent.
caveat: Excludes non-controlling interests and is therefore NOT the counterpart of ifrs-full:Equity; it corresponds to ifrs-full:EquityAttributableToOwnersOfParent. It is second here because many filings tag no total including NCI, not because it is equivalent.

basis: Equity attributable to the owners of the parent.
親会社の所有者に帰属する持分（IFRS）, the counterpart of ifrs-full:EquityAttributableToOwnersOfParent.
caveat: A report that prepares consolidated statements states this figure twice, the group's with no dimension on the context and the parent company's own under NonConsolidatedMember, and both are in the table of facts. A query that does not say which it wants gets two sets of accounts at once.

basis: Equity attributable to the parent; the counterpart of the IFRS element.
Total liabilities as IAS 1 presents it.
負債（IFRS）, total liabilities.
caveat: A report that prepares consolidated statements states this figure twice, the group's with no dimension on the context and the parent company's own under NonConsolidatedMember, and both are in the table of facts. A query that does not say which it wants gets two sets of accounts at once.

basis: 負債, total liabilities.
caveat: A report that prepares consolidated statements states this figure twice, the group's with no dimension on the context and the parent company's own under NonConsolidatedMember, and both are in the table of facts. A query that does not say which it wants gets two sets of accounts at once.

basis: Total liabilities as ASC 210 presents it.
caveat: Many filings with the Commission tag no total liabilities at all, presenting only liabilities and equity together, so this measure is absent for a substantial part of the US population rather than zero.

basis: Profit or loss including non-controlling interests as IAS 1 presents it.
当期利益（IFRS）, the result for the year including the share of the non-controlling interests.
caveat: Of the continuing and the discontinued operations together, which is what ifrs-full:ProfitLoss means; the result before tax that a Japanese IFRS statement presents is of the continuing operations alone. A report that prepares consolidated statements states this figure twice, the group's with no dimension on the context and the parent company's own under NonConsolidatedMember, and both are in the table of facts. A query that does not say which it wants gets two sets of accounts at once.

basis: 当期純利益, the result for the year including the share of the non-controlling interests; the counterpart of ifrs-full:ProfitLoss.
caveat: A report that prepares consolidated statements states this figure twice, the group's with no dimension on the context and the parent company's own under NonConsolidatedMember, and both are in the table of facts. A query that does not say which it wants gets two sets of accounts at once.

basis: Net income including non-controlling interests, which is what ifrs-full:ProfitLoss means.
Net income attributable to the parent.
caveat: Excludes non-controlling interests and is therefore NOT the counterpart of ifrs-full:ProfitLoss; it corresponds to ifrs-full:ProfitLossAttributableToOwnersOfParent. It is second here because many filings tag no total including NCI.

basis: Profit or loss attributable to the owners of the parent.
親会社の所有者、当期利益（IFRS）, the result attributable to the owners of the parent.
caveat: A report that prepares consolidated statements states this figure twice, the group's with no dimension on the context and the parent company's own under NonConsolidatedMember, and both are in the table of facts. A query that does not say which it wants gets two sets of accounts at once.

basis: 親会社株主に帰属する当期純利益, the result attributable to the shareholders of the parent.
caveat: A filer that prepares no consolidated statements has no non-controlling interest and states no such line; its result is jppfs_cor:ProfitLoss and the two measures are the same figure. A report that prepares consolidated statements states this figure twice, the group's with no dimension on the context and the parent company's own under NonConsolidatedMember, and both are in the table of facts. A query that does not say which it wants gets two sets of accounts at once.

basis: Net income attributable to the parent; the counterpart of the IFRS element.
Revenue as IAS 1 requires it to be presented.
caveat: Broader than the US element: ifrs-full:Revenue may include revenue from sources other than contracts with customers, which ASC 606 reports separately.

basis: 売上収益（IFRS）, revenue under IFRS 15.
caveat: A report that prepares consolidated statements states this figure twice, the group's with no dimension on the context and the parent company's own under NonConsolidatedMember, and both are in the table of facts. A query that does not say which it wants gets two sets of accounts at once.

basis: Revenue from contracts with customers under IFRS 15; the exact counterpart of the ASC 606 element.
caveat: Excludes revenue outside IFRS 15 that the total may include.

basis: 売上高, net sales.
caveat: A filer whose revenue is 営業収益 rather than 売上高 -- a railway, a utility, an insurer -- states it under another element, and no row here reaches it: none of the reports this catalogue was written against uses one, and an element nobody has seen in a conversion is not put in an accounting catalogue. A report that prepares consolidated statements states this figure twice, the group's with no dimension on the context and the parent company's own under NonConsolidatedMember, and both are in the table of facts. A query that does not say which it wants gets two sets of accounts at once.

basis: Revenue from contracts with customers under ASC 606; IFRS 15 and ASC 606 are substantially converged.
caveat: The excluding and including assessed tax split has no IFRS counterpart; a filer choosing the including variant is reporting a larger figure than an IFRS filer would.

basis: The same revenue with assessed taxes included where the filer tags only this one.
caveat: Larger than the IFRS measure by the assessed taxes it includes.

basis: Total revenues where the filer tags no ASC 606 element.
caveat: Predates ASC 606 and is tagged inconsistently; it is the last resort and not an equivalent of the IFRS total.
